verdict.analysis: Both remove the insecure image, repair navigation and CTAs, add descriptions, and deliver readable layouts with accessible text replacing imagery. Neither establishes launch readiness: both invent package names and SDK APIs unsupported by the supplied files, then leave confirmation to the owner. Their claimed tests have no observable execution evidence. A additionally introduces an invalid relative-URL sitemap and unfinished social metadata; its report is unnecessarily expansive. B delivers a more focused result and clearer blocker record. The original files provide no established palette to verify either redesign against.

criteria.note: Both remove the HTTP image and use local resources.
Neither retains content images requiring alt text; examples are readable HTML text and decorative marks are hidden.
Both supply guide.html; A's get-started fragment also exists. Documentation accuracy remains a separate blocker.
Both link to an existing api.html.
Primary CTAs resolve to the supplied guide rather than a dead # link.
Both use clear quickstart and API labels matching their destinations.
Both add relevant homepage meta descriptions and explanatory product copy.
